How does Love speak?
And in the pallor that succeeds it; by The quivering lid of an averted eye--
Thus doth Love speak.
By the uneven heart-throbs, and the freak Of bounding pulses that stand still and ache,
Along vein-channels their disturbing course; Still as the dawn, and with the dawn's swift force--
How does Love speak?
The sudden silence and reserve when near-- The eye that glistens with an unshed tear--
As the alarmed heart leaps in the breast, And knows and names and greets its godlike guest--
How does Love speak?
The haughty heart grown humble; in the tender And unnamed light that floods the world with splendor;
In all fair things to one beloved face; In the shy touch of hands that thrill and tremble;
Thus doth Love speak.
In the wild words that uttered seem so weak They shrink ashamed to silence; in the fire Glance strikes with glance, swift flashing high and higher
In the deep, soulful stillness; in the warm, Impassioned tide that sweeps through throbbing veins
In the embrace where madness melts in bliss, And in the convulsive rapture of a kiss--
How can I wait until you come to me?
Their sunny smiles touched with malicious glee At my unrest; they seem to pause, and play
How can I wait?
Refused to pause or loiter with me long; But now they idly fill their hands with flowers,
The summer blooms, not heeding my one song, How can I wait?
They reach forth to a future day, and bring Sweet dreams of you to people all my mind;
I feast upon your face, I no more sing, How can I wait?
A pitying night has flung upon my soul. You are not near me, and I know full well
Before we meet, hours, days, and weeks must roll. How can I wait?
Until the sunlight of your eyes shall shine Upon my world that seems so desolate?
Until you come again, oh, love of mine, How can I wait?
When my blood flows calm as a purling river,
It is then that I vow we must part forever, That I will forget you, and put you away
Out of the mind when the dreamer awakes; That I know it will be, when the spell has vanished,
When the court of the mind is ruled by Reason,
But Love is a spy who is plotting treason, In league with that warm, red rebel, the Heart.
That his reign is wicked, his law a sin; And every word they utter is fuel
And on nights like this, when my blood runs riot
When my brain in vain bids my heart be quiet, When my breast seems the centre of lava-fires,
And I swear by the stars and my soul and say That I will have you and hold you and kiss you,
And like Communists, as mad, as disloyal,
They hate King Reason for being royal; They would fire his castle, and burn him there. Oh, Love! they would clasp you and crush you and kill you,
Across the miles, does this wild war thrill you That is raging in my soul?
